olbia.t: Milesian colony on the Bug-Dnieper estuary that was the main Greek gateway to the Scythians, described first-hand by Herodotus.
olbia.o: [[e:greeks|Greeks]] from [[s:miletus|Miletus]] first settled on Berezan island in the 7th century BCE, and around 550 BCE founded [[s:olbia-pontica|Olbia]] ('the prosperous') on the right bank of the [[e:southern-bug|Hypanis]] (Southern Bug) estuary. Its people also called it Borysthenes, after the [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]]. The colony took over much of the fertile surrounding steppe edge.
olbia.r: [[s:olbia-pontica|Olbia]] traded wine, [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]] and fine pottery to the [[e:scythians|Scythians]] for grain, fish, hides and slaves, and lived alongside Scythian rulers, one of whom, [[e:scyles|Scyles]], kept a house there. A self-governing polis, it worshipped [[e:apollo-delphinios|Apollo Delphinios]] and [[e:achilles|Achilles]], and issued early cast bronze money shaped like dolphins. [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] visited in the 5th century BCE.
olbia.e: [[s:olbia-pontica|Olbia]] resisted a siege by Alexander's general [[e:zopyrion|Zopyrion]] c. 331 BCE but declined in the later [[e:hellenistic-period|Hellenistic period]]. Around 55 BCE the [[s:getae|Getae]] under [[e:burebista|Burebista]] sacked it. It was later rebuilt on a smaller scale under Roman protection and abandoned in the 4th century CE. The ruins near Parutyne in [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]] are a protected reserve.

orange-free-state.t: The Boer republic between the Orange and Vaal rivers, admired for its stable constitution, which fell with its ally the Transvaal in 1902.
orange-free-state.o: When [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] gave up the [[s:orange-river-sovereignty|Orange River Sovereignty]], the [[e:bloemfontein-convention|Bloemfontein Convention]] of 23 February 1854 recognised the [[e:burghers|burghers]]' independence. They adopted a constitution with an elected president and [[e:volksraad-dutch-east-indies|Volksraad]] and kept [[e:bloemfontein|Bloemfontein]] as their capital.
orange-free-state.r: Citizenship was limited to white men, but the state gained a reputation for orderly government, especially under President [[e:johannes-brand|Johannes Brand]] from 1864 to 1888. Wars with the [[s:basotho-kingdom|Basotho Kingdom]] won fertile land in the [[e:caledon-river|Caledon]] valley. [[e:britain|Britain's]] seizure of the diamond fields of [[s:griqualand-west|Griqualand West]] was settled with a payment of £90,000 in 1876. Farming of sheep and grain dominated the economy.
orange-free-state.e: Under President [[e:martinus-theunis-steyn|Martinus Theunis Steyn]] the Free State joined the [[s:south-african-republic|South African Republic]] against [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1899. [[e:britain|Britain]] annexed it in 1900, and the 1902 [[e:treaty-of-vereeniging|Treaty of Vereeniging]] confirmed it as the [[s:orange-river-colony|Orange River Colony]].

oneida-nation.t: The People of the Standing Stone, one of the five founding nations of the Iroquois Confederacy, and the main Haudenosaunee ally of the Americans in the Revolution.
oneida-nation.o: The Oneida took shape as a nation in central [[e:new-york|New York]] around [[e:oneida-lake|Oneida Lake]] and Oneida [[e:muscogee|Creek]], their name recalling a boulder that marked their principal settlement. Around the mid-15th century, according to [[s:iroquois-confederacy|Haudenosaunee]] tradition, they joined the [[s:mohawk-nation|Mohawk]], [[s:onondaga-nation|Onondaga]], [[s:cayuga-nation|Cayuga]] and [[s:seneca-nation|Seneca]] in accepting the [[e:great-law-of-peace|Great Law of Peace]], forming the Iroquois [[s:confederate-states-of-america|Confederacy]].
oneida-nation.r: Like the other member nations, the Oneida were organised in clans, with women owning the longhouses and fields and clan mothers selecting the chiefs who represented the nation, nine of them, at the [[e:grand-council-qing|Grand Council]]. Villages farmed [[e:maize|maize]], beans and squash and traded [[e:fur-trade|furs]]. In council they sat with the [[s:cayuga-nation|Cayuga]] as the younger brothers. Influenced by the Presbyterian missionary [[e:samuel-kirkland|Samuel Kirkland]], many converted to [[e:christianity|Christianity]] in the 18th century.
oneida-nation.e: In the [[e:american-revolution|American Revolution]] the Oneida fought for the Americans at [[e:battle-of-oriskany|Oriskany]] and sent corn to Valley Forge, yet lost most of their land through [[e:new-york|New York]] State treaties. Many moved to [[e:wisconsin|Wisconsin]] in the 1820s and to [[e:ontario|Ontario]] in 1840. Today there are Oneida nations in New [[e:york-maine|York]], Wisconsin and Ontario.

odessos.t: Milesian colony on the Bay of Varna that linked Thracian kingdoms to Aegean trade for five centuries and grew into modern Varna.
odessos.o: Odessos was founded by colonists from [[s:miletus|Miletus]] on the western [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] coast, usually dated to c. 585-570 BCE, at the mouth of a valley leading inland towards [[e:thrace|Thrace]]. The site had good anchorage and access to fertile land, and the colony grew through exchange with the Thracian [[s:getae|Getae]] and [[e:odrysians|Odrysians]] of the interior.
odessos.r: Odessos was a self-governing Greek polis whose prosperity rested on grain, fish, wine imports and trade with Thracian rulers, whose wealth appears in rich local tombs. Its chief deity was the Great God, a Hellenised form of the Thracian [[e:darzalas|Darzalas]], shown on its coins. It probably took part in the revolt of the West Pontic cities against [[e:lysimachus|Lysimachus]] in 313 BCE.
odessos.e: Like [[s:tomis|Tomis]], [[s:callatis|Callatis]] and [[s:mesembria|Mesembria]], Odessos came under Roman control after the campaign of [[e:marcus-terentius-varro-lucullus|Marcus Terentius Varro Lucullus]] in 72-71 BCE. As Odessus it prospered in the Roman province of [[e:moesia|Moesia]], with large public baths, and later passed to [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] and the [[e:bulgarians|Bulgarians]]. The modern city is [[e:varna|Varna]].
odessos.re: Ancient Greek religion (cult of the Great God)

old-kingdom-of-egypt.t: Egypt of the Third to Sixth Dynasties, the age of the pyramids and of an all-powerful god-king ruling from Memphis.
old-kingdom-of-egypt.o: The Old Kingdom began around 2686 BCE with the [[e:third-dynasty-of-egypt|Third Dynasty]], which followed [[s:early-dynastic-egypt|Early Dynastic Egypt]]. Its king [[e:djoser|Djoser]] and his official [[e:imhotep|Imhotep]] built the [[e:pyramid-of-djoser|Step Pyramid]] at [[e:saqqara|Saqqara]], the first monumental stone building, and the kings of the Fourth Dynasty turned the experiment into true pyramids.
old-kingdom-of-egypt.r: [[e:sneferu|Sneferu]] built the pyramids at [[e:dahshur|Dahshur]] and [[e:meidum|Meidum]], and his son [[e:khufu|Khufu]] raised the [[e:great-pyramid-of-giza|Great Pyramid]] at [[e:giza|Giza]], followed by [[e:khafre|Khafre]] and [[e:menkaure|Menkaure]]. A literate bureaucracy headed by the [[e:vizier|vizier]] taxed grain and organised labour on a vast scale. The Fifth Dynasty favoured the sun god Ra with sun temples, and Unas had the [[e:pyramid-texts|Pyramid Texts]] carved in his tomb. Expeditions sought turquoise in Sinai and [[e:incense|incense]] in [[e:land-of-punt|Punt]].
old-kingdom-of-egypt.e: Under the Sixth Dynasty, provincial governors (nomarchs) grew powerful and hereditary, and the very long reign of [[e:pepi-ii|Pepi II]] was followed by weakness, possibly worsened by low [[e:nile|Nile]] floods. Central authority faded around 2181 BCE, leaving the short-lived [[s:eighth-dynasty-of-egypt|Eighth Dynasty of Egypt]] and the [[e:first-intermediate-period|First Intermediate Period]].

old-great-bulgaria.t: Khan Kubrat's short-lived Bulgar state north of the Black Sea, whose break-up sent Bulgars to the Danube and the Volga.
old-great-bulgaria.o: In the 630s [[e:kubrat|Kubrat]] of the [[e:dulo-clan|Dulo clan]] threw off the overlordship of the [[e:avars|Avars]] and united the [[e:onogurs|Onogur]] and [[e:bulgars|Bulgar]] tribes of the steppe between the Kuban and the lower [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]]. Raised partly at the court of [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] and baptised there, he made an alliance with the emperor [[e:heraclius|Heraclius]], who gave him the title of patrician.
old-great-bulgaria.r: Great Bulgaria was a confederation of Turkic-speaking nomadic tribes ruled by a khan of the [[e:dulo-clan|Dulo clan]], with [[e:phanagoria|Phanagoria]] on the Taman peninsula as a centre. Its wealth is shown by the treasure of [[e:pereshchepina-treasure|Malaya Pereshchepina]] in [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]], often identified as [[e:kubrat|Kubrat's]] burial, with gold and [[e:silver|silver]] vessels and Byzantine gifts.
old-great-bulgaria.e: After [[e:kubrat|Kubrat]] died around 665, his sons divided the people as [[e:khazar-khaganate|Khazar]] pressure grew. Batbayan stayed and submitted to the Khazars, [[e:kotrag|Kotrag]] led his followers north to found [[s:volga-bulgaria|Volga Bulgaria]], and [[e:asparuh-of-bulgaria|Asparukh]] moved to the [[e:danube|Danube]], where he founded the [[s:first-bulgarian-empire|First Bulgarian Empire]] in 681.

olbia-pontica.t: The leading Greek city on the northern Black Sea coast, a trading gateway between the Mediterranean world and the Scythian steppe.
olbia-pontica.o: Colonists from [[s:miletus|Miletus]] founded [[s:olbia|Olbia]], meaning 'prosperous', around 550 BCE on the estuary of the [[e:southern-bug|Southern Bug]], near an older Greek trading post on Berezan island. The site, close to the mouth of the [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]], gave access to the grain lands and river routes of [[s:scythia|Scythia]].
olbia-pontica.r: [[s:olbia|Olbia]] was a democratic polis with an assembly, council and annual magistrates, and it cast distinctive bronze coins shaped like dolphins. Its merchants exported grain, fish and slaves and imported wine, oil and luxury goods. [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] visited the city, and his story of the Scythian king [[e:scyles|Scyles]], who secretly lived as a Greek there, shows how closely the two worlds mixed.
olbia-pontica.e: [[s:olbia|Olbia]] resisted a siege by Alexander's general [[e:zopyrion|Zopyrion]] in 331 BCE but was badly sacked by the [[s:getae|Getae]] around 55 BCE. Rebuilt on a smaller scale, it came under Roman protection in the 2nd century CE. Gothic attacks in the 3rd century and the Hunnic invasion in the 4th brought urban life to an end.

osroene.t: Osroene, the kingdom of Edessa in upper Mesopotamia, cradle of Syriac literature and one of the earliest centres of Christianity.
osroene.o: As the [[s:seleucid-empire|Seleucid Empire]] lost its eastern lands, a local dynasty of Arab origin took power at [[s:county-of-edessa|Edessa]], modern [[e:sanliurfa|Şanlıurfa]], c. 132 BCE. Its kings, many called Abgar or Ma'nu, ruled a small kingdom between the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] and [[e:khabur-river|Khabur]], balancing [[e:rome|Rome]] and the [[s:parthian-empire|Parthian Empire]].
osroene.r: [[s:county-of-edessa|Edessa]] grew rich on the trade crossing the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]]. Its kings wrote in [[e:syriac|Syriac]], an [[e:aramaic|Aramaic]] dialect that became a great literary language. A legend told of King [[e:abgar-v|Abgar V]] corresponding with [[e:jesus|Jesus]], and [[e:christianity|Christianity]] spread early; [[e:abgar-viii|Abgar VIII]] is often said to have converted, though this is debated.
osroene.e: [[e:caracalla|Caracalla]] deposed the king in 214 CE and made Osroene a Roman colony. The dynasty was briefly restored but ended under Abgar X in the 240s, and the kingdom became a Roman province.

opuntian-locris.t: Confederation of the eastern Locrians on the Euboean Gulf, centred on Opus and remembered for the Locrian maidens sent to Troy.
opuntian-locris.o: The eastern [[e:locrians|Locrians]] lived along the coast of central [[e:greece|Greece]] facing [[e:euboea|Euboea]], separated from their western kin in [[s:ozolian-locris|Ozolian Locris]] by [[e:doris-greece|Doris]] and [[e:phocis|Phocis]]. [[e:homer|Homer]] placed [[e:ajax-the-lesser|Ajax the Lesser]] among them. By the Archaic period their towns formed a confederation led by Opus, governed by an oligarchic council of a thousand.
opuntian-locris.r: The [[e:locrians|Locrians]] kept old customs, such as sending two noble maidens each year to serve [[e:athena|Athena]] at [[e:troy|Ilion]] in atonement for [[e:ajax-the-lesser|Ajax]]'s sacrilege. An early 5th century BCE bronze tablet records the terms for Locrian colonists at [[e:nafpaktos|Naupactus]]. They fought with [[e:leonidas-i|Leonidas]] at [[e:battle-of-thermopylae|Thermopylae]] in 480 BCE, then were forced to join the [[e:persians|Persians]], and later usually sided with [[s:thebes|Thebes]] and [[s:sparta|Sparta]] against [[s:athens|Athens]].
opuntian-locris.e: The [[s:phocian-league|Phocian League]] overran much of the region in the [[e:third-sacred-war|Third Sacred War]]. Eastern [[e:locris|Locris]] later passed under Macedonian, Boeotian and [[s:aetolian-league|Aetolian League]] control and came under [[e:rome|Rome]] in 146 BCE.

oghuz-yabgu-state.t: The Oghuz Turkic state of the lower Syr Darya and Aral steppe, cradle of the Seljuks and of the Turkmen.
oghuz-yabgu-state.o: The [[e:oghuz-turks|Oghuz]] tribes moved from the eastern steppe to the lower [[e:syr-darya|Syr Darya]] and the [[e:aral-sea|Aral]] region in the 8th century, after the fall of the [[s:western-turkic-khaganate|Western Turkic Khaganate]] and wars with the [[s:karluk-yabgu|Karluks]]. By the 9th century they formed a confederation led by a ruler with the title yabghu.
oghuz-yabgu-state.r: The yabghu ruled from [[e:yangikent|Yangikent]] near the mouth of the [[e:syr-darya|Syr Darya]], a winter capital among nomadic pastures. The traveller [[e:ahmad-ibn-fadlan|Ibn Fadlan]], who crossed their lands in 922, described their customs, military leaders and lack of [[e:islam|Islam]]. They traded with [[e:khwarazm|Khwarazm]] and the [[s:samanid-empire|Samanid Empire]], and fought the [[s:pechenegs|Pechenegs]] and the [[e:khazar-khaganate|Khazars]]. Islam spread among them in the 10th century.
oghuz-yabgu-state.e: Internal splits weakened the state; the Seljuk clan broke away to the south and conquered [[e:iran|Iran]] from 1037. Around the mid-11th century the remaining [[e:oghuz-turks|Oghuz]] were pushed west by the [[e:kipchaks|Kipchaks]] of the [[s:kimek-khanate|Kimek Khanate]], some becoming the [[s:torks|Torks]] of the [[e:russia|Russian steppe]], others the [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]].

olba.t: Olba, a priestly principality in the hills of Rough Cilicia, ruled by high priests of Zeus who claimed descent from the hero Teucer.
olba.o: Olba grew around the sanctuary of [[e:zeus|Zeus]] Olbios at [[e:uzuncaburc|Uzuncaburç]], in the mountains above the Cilician coast. In the [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucid]] period it was governed by a line of high priests, the Teucrids, who traced their descent to [[e:teucer|Teucer]], a hero of the [[e:trojan-war|Trojan War]], and ruled the surrounding temple lands.
olba.r: The priest-kings controlled a territory of villages and forests from fortified towers. The temple of [[e:zeus|Zeus]], built in the 3rd century BCE, still stands among later ruins. In the 1st century BCE the dynasty was disrupted by usurpers such as Zenophanes, whose daughter Aba won Roman favour.
olba.e: Under Augustus the Teucrid Ajax son of [[e:teucer|Teucer]] ruled as high priest and toparch. A king Polemon, probably [[e:polemon-ii-of-pontus|Polemon II of Pontus]], later held Olba, and Vespasian absorbed it into Roman [[e:cilicia|Cilicia]] in 72 CE; the sanctuary town became [[e:uzuncaburc|Diocaesarea]].

orlam-afrikaner-state.t: Jonker Afrikaner's horse-riding, gun-using Oorlam state that dominated central Namibia and founded Windhoek.
orlam-afrikaner-state.o: The [[e:afrikaners|Afrikaners]] were an [[e:oorlam|Oorlam]] group, [[e:khoekhoe|Khoekhoe]] of the Cape frontier who had adopted horses, guns and [[e:cape-dutch|Cape Dutch]], led by [[e:jager-afrikaner|Jager Afrikaner]]. Around 1823 his son [[e:jonker-afrikaner|Jonker Afrikaner]] moved north at the invitation of the [[e:nama-people|Nama]] to help them against the [[e:herero-people|Herero]], and by about 1840 he had settled at [[e:windhoek|Windhoek]], which he made his capital.
orlam-afrikaner-state.r: [[e:jonker-afrikaner|Jonker]]'s mounted gunmen raided [[e:herero-people|Herero]] [[e:cattle|cattle]] and controlled trade routes to [[e:walvis-bay|Walvis Bay]], where cattle were exchanged for guns, horses and brandy. He welcomed Wesleyan and Rhenish missionaries, built a road to the coast and ruled a large following of [[e:oorlam|Oorlam]], [[e:nama-people|Nama]] and dependent Herero. His power rested on firearms and alliances rather than on a fixed territory.
orlam-afrikaner-state.e: After [[e:jonker-afrikaner|Jonker]]'s death in 1861 and his son Christian's death in battle at [[e:otjimbingwe|Otjimbingwe]] in 1863, the [[e:herero-people|Herero]] under [[e:maharero|Maharero]] won their independence. [[e:jan-jonker-afrikaner|Jan Jonker Afrikaner]] was finally defeated by the Herero in 1880, and the group lost its land.

odawara-domain.t: The domain guarding the Hakone pass on the Tokaido road at the former Later Hojo capital, held mostly by the Okubo family.
odawara-domain.o: After [[e:toyotomi-hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] took [[e:odawara|Odawara]] from the Later Hojo in 1590, [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] gave the castle to his senior retainer [[e:okubo-tadayo|Okubo Tadayo]]. His son [[e:okubo-tadachika|Tadachika]] was dismissed in 1614 in a court intrigue, and the domain passed through other hands, including the Inaba family from 1632.
odawara-domain.r: [[e:odawara|Odawara]] controlled the approaches to the [[e:hakone-checkpoint|Hakone checkpoint]], the key control point on the road between [[e:edo-tokyo|Edo]] and [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]]. The Okubo returned in 1686. The eruption of [[e:mount-fuji|Mount Fuji]] in 1707 buried much of its farmland in ash. In the early 19th century [[e:okubo-tadazane|Okubo Tadazane]] employed the agrarian reformer [[e:ninomiya-sontoku|Ninomiya Sontoku]] to restore ruined villages.
odawara-domain.e: During the [[e:boshin-war|Boshin War]] [[e:odawara|Odawara]] wavered between the [[e:shogun|shogunate]] and the new government before submitting in 1868. After the abolition of the domains in 1871 it was absorbed into [[e:kanagawa-prefecture|Kanagawa Prefecture]].

orchomenus-boeotia.t: Ancient Boeotian city, heir of Mycenaean Orchomenos, which rivalled Thebes for leadership of Boeotia until the Thebans destroyed it in 364 BCE.
orchomenus-boeotia.o: After the collapse of the [[s:mycenaean-kingdom-of-orchomenos|Mycenaean Kingdom of Orchomenos]] c. 1200 BCE, the town survived beside the refilled [[e:lake-copais|Lake Copais]]. In the [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] it became a Boeotian polis and the main rival of [[s:thebes|Thebes]], sometimes leading western [[e:boeotia|Boeotia]]. Its cult of the [[e:charites|Graces]], the Charites, was among the oldest in [[e:greece|Greece]].
orchomenus-boeotia.r: Orchomenus was a member of the [[s:boeotian-league|Boeotian League]] and an oligarchy of landowners. It sided with [[s:sparta|Sparta]] against [[s:thebes|Thebes]] in the early 4th century BCE and fought at [[e:battle-of-coronea-394-bc|Coronea]] in 394 BCE. Its festival of the Charitesia attracted poets and musicians, and [[e:pindar|Pindar]] wrote an ode for an Orchomenian victor.
orchomenus-boeotia.e: [[s:thebes|Thebes]] destroyed Orchomenus in 364 BCE, killing its men. [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]] rebuilt it after [[e:battle-of-chaeronea-338-bce|Chaeronea]] in 338 BCE. [[e:sulla|Sulla]] defeated [[e:mithridates-vi-of-pontus|Mithridates]]'s army nearby in 85 BCE, and the town, under [[e:rome|Rome]] from 146 BCE, continued on a smaller scale.
orchomenus-boeotia.re: Greek religion; cult of the Charites

omagua.t: A powerful riverine chiefdom on the upper Amazon whose dense villages amazed the first Spanish explorers in the 16th century.
omagua.o: The Omagua, a Tupi-Guarani-speaking people, settled along the [[e:amazon|Amazon]], known locally as the [[e:solimoes|Solimões]], and its islands between the [[e:napo-river|Napo]] and [[e:jurua-river|Juruá]] rivers. Their expansion along the river is dated archaeologically to around 1000.
omagua.r: [[e:gaspar-de-carvajal|Gaspar de Carvajal]], who accompanied [[e:francisco-de-orellana|Francisco de Orellana's]] voyage down the [[e:amazon|Amazon]] in 1542, described the territory of a chief called Machiparo and densely populated villages lining the riverbanks. The Omagua farmed manioc and [[e:maize|maize]] on the fertile floodplain, kept turtles in pens and traded goods along the river. They flattened the foreheads of infants as a mark of status. They were noted for fine painted pottery and [[e:cotton|cotton]] cloth.
omagua.e: Slave raids from [[s:colonial-brazil|Portuguese Brazil]], epidemics and the missions of the [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] [[e:samuel-fritz|Samuel Fritz]] around 1700 broke up the chiefdom. Survivors moved upriver into Spanish territory, settling around San Joaquín de Omaguas in [[e:peru|Peru]]. A few communities, also known as Cambeba, survive in Peru and [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]].

okayama-domain.t: The domain of Bizen, whose Confucian lord Ikeda Mitsumasa founded one of Japan's first schools for commoners and whose heirs built the Korakuen garden.
okayama-domain.o: [[e:kobayakawa-hideaki|Kobayakawa Hideaki]], whose defection decided the battle of [[e:battle-of-sekigahara|Sekigahara]], received [[e:okayama|Okayama]] in 1600 but died without an heir in 1602. The Ikeda family then took over, and in 1632 [[e:ikeda-mitsumasa|Ikeda Mitsumasa]] moved there from [[e:tottori|Tottori]], exchanging domains with his cousin.
okayama-domain.r: [[e:ikeda-mitsumasa|Mitsumasa]], a committed Confucian, employed the scholar [[e:kumazawa-banzan|Kumazawa Banzan]], promoted flood control and land reclamation, restricted Buddhist temples and in 1670 founded the Shizutani school, open to commoners. His son [[e:ikeda-tsunamasa|Ikeda Tsunamasa]] completed the [[e:koraku-en|Korakuen]] garden in 1700. The domain, of about 315,000 koku, produced [[e:rice|rice]], salt and [[e:cotton|cotton]] and [[e:bizen-ware|Bizen ware]].
okayama-domain.e: [[e:okayama|Okayama]] joined the imperial side in the [[e:boshin-war|Boshin War]] of 1868. After abolition in 1871 it became [[e:okayama-prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], and the Shizutani school building is now a national treasure.

old-swiss-confederacy.t: The loose alliance of Alpine cantons that grew from a 1291 pact into a neutral federation of thirteen members, the forerunner of modern Switzerland.
old-swiss-confederacy.o: Tradition dates the [[s:confederate-states-of-america|Confederacy]] to the [[e:federal-charter-of-1291|Federal Charter of August 1291]], a defensive pact between Uri, [[s:canton-of-schwyz|Schwyz]] and [[s:canton-of-unterwalden|Unterwalden]] against outside lords, above all the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]]. After victory over a [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] army at [[e:battle-of-morgarten|Morgarten]] in 1315, [[s:canton-of-lucerne|Lucerne]] (1332), [[s:canton-of-zurich|Zürich]] (1351), [[s:canton-of-glarus|Glarus]] and Zug (1352) and Bern (1353) joined; the victories at [[e:battle-of-sempach|Sempach]] in 1386 and [[e:battle-of-nafels|Näfels]] in 1388 secured the alliance, and by 1513 it numbered thirteen cantons.
old-swiss-confederacy.r: There was no central government. The cantons, a mix of rural assemblies and patrician city republics, sent envoys to the [[e:tagsatzung|Diet]] (Tagsatzung), which decided only by consensus. They jointly ruled subject territories and kept associates such as the [[s:three-leagues|Three Leagues]] and the [[s:republic-of-geneva|Republic of Geneva]]. Swiss [[e:pike|pikemen]] were [[e:europe|Europe's]] most sought-after [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]], and the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] split the cantons into Catholic and Reformed camps that fought several civil wars.
old-swiss-confederacy.e: Independence from the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]] was recognised at the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648. In 1798 French armies invaded and replaced the old order with the centralised [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]]. [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] [[e:act-of-mediation|Act of Mediation]] of 1803 restored a federation, from which the modern Swiss state developed.

oxybii.t: Ligurian people of the coast near Fréjus who, with the Deciates, provoked Rome's first intervention beyond the Alps in 154 BCE.
oxybii.o: Known chiefly from [[e:polybius|Polybius]], the Oxybii lived on the coast west of [[e:antibes|Antibes]], near the port of [[e:aegitna|Aegitna]], probably around modern [[e:mandelieu-la-napoule|Mandelieu]] or [[e:cannes|Cannes]].
oxybii.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers. [[e:polybius|Polybius]] tells that they attacked Roman envoys landing at [[e:aegitna|Aegitna]] and wounded one of them.
oxybii.e: In 154 BCE the consul [[e:quintus-opimius|Quintus Opimius]] marched against them, took [[e:aegitna|Aegitna]] and defeated them and the [[s:deciates|Deciates]]. Their land was given to [[s:massalia|Massalia]] and later absorbed into [[e:gallia-narbonensis|Gallia Narbonensis]], where the Roman colony of [[e:frejus|Forum Julii]] (Fréjus) was founded nearby.

ottoman-tunisia.t: Tunis as an Ottoman province, where power shifted from pashas to Janissary deys and then to the hereditary Muradid beys.
ottoman-tunisia.o: In 1574 an Ottoman expedition under [[e:koca-sinan-pasha|Sinan Pasha]] took [[e:tunis|Tunis]] and [[e:la-goulette|La Goulette]] from [[e:spain|Spain]] and its [[e:hafsid-dynasty|Hafsid]] client, ending the [[s:hafsid-sultanate|Hafsid Sultanate]]. [[e:tunisia|Tunisia]] became a province of the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] under a pasha, with a strong [[e:janissaries|Janissary]] garrison.
ottoman-tunisia.r: A [[e:janissaries|Janissary]] revolt in 1591 put power in the hands of deys, notably [[e:uthman-dey|Uthman Dey]] and [[e:yusuf-dey|Yusuf Dey]], who welcomed [[e:moriscos|Morisco]] refugees from [[e:spain|Spain]] after 1609; they founded towns such as [[e:testour|Testour]]. Corsairing and [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] trade brought wealth. Meanwhile the beys, commanders of the tax-collecting army, grew stronger, and Murad Bey's descendants, the [[e:muradid-dynasty|Muradids]], became hereditary rulers under [[e:hammuda-pasha-bey|Hammuda Pasha Bey]].
ottoman-tunisia.e: [[e:muradid-dynasty|Muradid]] succession wars from 1675 and invasions from the [[s:regency-of-algiers|Regency of Algiers]] weakened the state. In 1702 the Muradid line was destroyed, and in 1705 [[e:husayn-ibn-ali|Husayn ibn Ali]] seized power, founding the [[s:beylik-of-tunis|Husainid dynasty]] of the [[e:beylik|Beylik]] of [[e:tunis|Tunis]].

olynthus.t: Chief city of Chalcidice, head of the Chalcidian League, whose destruction by Philip II in 348 BCE left the best-preserved classical Greek town plan.
olynthus.o: Olynthus stood on hills near the head of the [[e:gulf-of-kassandra|Toronaic Gulf]]. It was a town of the [[e:bottiaeans|Bottiaeans]] until 479 BCE, when the Persian commander [[e:artabazus-i-of-phrygia|Artabazus]] massacred its people and handed it to Chalcidian [[e:greeks|Greeks]] under Critobulus of Torone. In 432 BCE many Chalcidians abandoned their coastal towns to settle there, at the urging of [[e:perdiccas-ii-of-macedon|Perdiccas II of Macedon]].
olynthus.r: Olynthus became the centre of the [[s:chalcidian-league|Chalcidian League]], a federal state with shared citizenship and coinage of fine [[e:silver|silver]]. A new town on a regular grid of blocks was built on the North Hill; excavations led by [[e:david-moore-robinson|David Robinson]] in the 1920s and 1930s uncovered whole houses with courtyards, mosaics and household goods, a rich picture of daily life.
olynthus.e: [[s:sparta|Sparta]] forced the league to submit after a war in 382-379 BCE. Restored, Olynthus became [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]]'s main rival in the north. Despite [[e:demosthenes|Demosthenes]]' [[e:olynthiacs|Olynthiac speeches]] urging Athenian help, Philip took the city by treachery in 348 BCE, razed it and sold its people into [[e:slavery|slavery]].

orange-river-colony.t: The British colony that replaced the Orange Free State after the Second Boer War, until it joined the Union of South Africa.
orange-river-colony.o: British forces took [[e:bloemfontein|Bloemfontein]] in March 1900, and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] proclaimed the annexation of the [[s:orange-free-state|Orange Free State]] as the Orange River Colony in May 1900. [[e:boers|Boer]] commandos fought on until the [[e:treaty-of-vereeniging|Treaty of Vereeniging]] in May 1902, when British rule became effective.
orange-river-colony.r: During the war, farms were burned and [[e:boers|Boer]] women and children held in [[e:concentration-camp|concentration camps]], where thousands died, as did many black Africans in separate camps. Under [[e:alfred-milner|Lord Milner's]] reconstruction the colony was run by appointed officials. After the Liberal victory in [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], responsible government was granted in 1907, and the [[e:orangia-unie|Orangia Unie]] party under [[e:abraham-fischer|Abraham Fischer]] took office.
orange-river-colony.e: In 1910 the colony joined the [[s:union-of-south-africa|Union of South Africa]] as the [[e:orange-free-state-province|Orange Free State Province]], keeping [[e:bloemfontein|Bloemfontein]] as the seat of the [[e:appellate-division-of-the-supreme-court-of-south-africa|Appellate Division]], which made it the country's judicial capital.

otomo-clan-domain.t: The Kyushu domain of the Otomo of Bungo, whose lord Otomo Sorin became a Christian and sent Japan's first embassy to Rome.
otomo-clan-domain.o: The [[e:otomo-clan|Otomo]] had held [[e:bungo-province|Bungo]] in northeastern [[e:kyushu|Kyushu]] as military governors since the [[e:kamakura|Kamakura]] period. In the early 16th century they consolidated their power from Funai, and under [[e:otomo-sorin|Otomo Yoshishige]], later known as Sorin, who succeeded in 1550, they expanded across northern Kyushu.
otomo-clan-domain.r: At its height the domain controlled or claimed six provinces. Funai traded with [[e:ming-empire|Ming China]] and with the Portuguese, and [[e:otomo-sorin|Sorin]] welcomed [[e:francis-xavier|Francis Xavier]] in 1551, protected [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] missionaries and was baptised in 1578. With other Christian lords he sponsored the [[e:tensho-embassy|Tensho embassy]] of young Japanese nobles to [[e:rome|Rome]], which left in 1582. Funai had a hospital and a Jesuit college.
otomo-clan-domain.e: The [[e:shimazu-clan|Shimazu]] crushed the [[e:otomo-clan|Otomo]] at [[e:battle-of-mimikawa|Mimikawa]] in 1578 and later invaded [[e:bungo-province|Bungo]]; [[e:otomo-sorin|Sorin]] appealed to [[e:toyotomi-hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi]], who conquered [[e:kyushu|Kyushu]] in 1587. Sorin's son [[e:otomo-yoshimune|Yoshimune]] was stripped of Bungo in 1593 for misconduct in the invasion of [[e:korea|Korea]].

ouetsu-reppan-domei.t: The alliance of some thirty northern domains formed in 1868 to resist the new Meiji government, the largest opposition in the Boshin War.
ouetsu-reppan-domei.o: After the [[e:shogun|shogunate]]'s defeat at [[e:battle-of-toba-fushimi|Toba-Fushimi]], the new government ordered northern domains to punish [[e:aizu|Aizu]] and Shonai. [[e:sendai|Sendai]] and [[e:yonezawa|Yonezawa]] sought pardon for them, and when this was refused, delegates met at [[e:shiroishi-miyagi|Shiroishi]] in May 1868 and formed an alliance, joined by Nagaoka and other [[e:echigo-province|Echigo]] domains.
ouetsu-reppan-domei.r: The alliance was a council of member domains rather than a state, with headquarters at [[e:shiroishi-miyagi|Shiroishi]] and leadership from [[e:sendai|Sendai]]. It invited Prince [[e:prince-kitashirakawa-yoshihisa|Rinnoji-no-miya Yoshihisa]], a member of the imperial family who had fled [[e:edo-tokyo|Edo]], to serve as its nominal head, presenting itself as loyal to the throne but opposed to [[e:satsuma-domain|Satsuma]] and [[e:choshu-domain|Choshu]].
ouetsu-reppan-domei.e: Kubota and others defected, Nagaoka fell, and [[e:yonezawa|Yonezawa]] and [[e:sendai|Sendai]] surrendered in October 1868, followed by [[e:aizu|Aizu]] and Shonai in November. Some alliance fighters joined the [[s:republic-of-ezo|Republic of Ezo]].

oiniwar-dynasty.t: A Maithil Brahmin dynasty that ruled Mithila for two centuries, famous as patrons of the poet Vidyapati.
oiniwar-dynasty.o: After the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]] overthrew the [[s:karnat-dynasty|Karnat dynasty]] in 1324, [[e:tughlaq-dynasty|Tughluq]] rulers granted [[e:mithila|Mithila]] to [[e:kameshwar-thakur|Kameshwar Thakur]], a [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] of the Oinwar family, to govern on their behalf. His descendants ruled the region north of the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]] as tributary kings, with seats at Sugauna and elsewhere.
oiniwar-dynasty.r: The Oiniwar kings were scholars as well as rulers and made [[e:mithila|Mithila]] a centre of [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] learning, especially [[e:nyaya|Nyaya]] logic. Their most famous protege was [[e:vidyapati|Vidyapati]], whose love songs in Maithili are classics of eastern Indian literature; he served kings such as Shivasimha. The kings balanced between the [[s:jaunpur-sultanate|Jaunpur Sultanate]] and the [[s:bengal-sultanate|Bengal Sultanate]].
oiniwar-dynasty.e: Weakened by wars with [[e:bengal|Bengal]] and the [[e:lodi-dynasty|Lodi]] sultans of [[e:delhi|Delhi]], the dynasty faded in the early 16th century, traditionally ending in 1526. [[e:mithila|Mithila]] later passed under the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]], which recognised the Khandavala family, the later [[e:raj-darbhanga|Raj Darbhanga]], as its leading landholders.

ordovices.t: Mountain peoples of north-west Wales who hosted Caratacus' last stand and fought Rome until Agricola crushed them in 77 or 78.
ordovices.o: The Ordovices held the uplands of [[e:snowdonia|Snowdonia]] and much of mid and north [[e:wales|Wales]], a region of small hillforts, stone-walled roundhouses and pastoral farming. They enter written history through [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]], who records that the British leader [[e:caratacus|Caratacus]] moved his war against [[e:rome|Rome]] into their territory around 51 after leaving the [[s:silures|Silures]].
ordovices.r: No coins, kings or towns are known, and power was probably held by local chiefs controlling upland grazing and fortified settlements. [[e:anglesey|Anglesey]], the island of Mona, lay on their borders and was a centre of the druids, whose sanctuary [[e:gaius-suetonius-paulinus|Suetonius Paulinus]] attacked in 60 before [[e:boudica|Boudica's]] revolt recalled him. Their resistance made the region one of the last parts of [[e:wales|Wales]] to be pacified.
ordovices.e: Around 77 the Ordovices destroyed a Roman cavalry unit. The new governor [[e:gnaeus-julius-agricola|Agricola]] answered with a campaign that, [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]] says, nearly wiped out the people, and then seized [[e:anglesey|Anglesey]]. Their land was held by forts such as [[e:segontium|Segontium]] at [[e:caernarfon|Caernarfon]], and no civitas of the Ordovices is known in [[s:roman-britain|Roman Britain]].

okjeo.t: A coastal people of northeastern Korea, known from Chinese records for their family ossuaries and tribute of fish and salt before Goguryeo absorbed them.
okjeo.o: Okjeo lay along the coast of what is now [[e:south-hamgyong-province|South Hamgyong]] province. After Han [[e:china|China]] conquered [[s:gojoseon|Gojoseon]] in 108 BCE the area was placed under the [[e:xuantu-commandery|Xuantu]] and then [[e:lelang-commandery|Lelang]] [[e:commandery|commanderies]], and Chinese writers distinguished an Eastern Okjeo on the coast from a Northern Okjeo further inland.
okjeo.r: Chinese historians describe villages led by hereditary chiefs with no overall king, farming fertile coastal land and paying tribute of fish, salt and seafood. Two customs stood out: girls were betrothed young and raised in their future husband's household, and the bones of a whole family were placed in a single large wooden coffin.
okjeo.e: [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] made Okjeo a tributary under King [[e:taejo-of-goguryeo|Taejo]], traditionally in 56 CE, and later absorbed it fully, drawing on its marine products. Okjeo's people merged into Goguryeo society.

orange-river-sovereignty.t: Britain's brief attempt to rule the land between the Orange and Vaal rivers, abandoned in 1854 in favour of the Orange Free State.
orange-river-sovereignty.o: [[e:sir-harry-smith-1st-baronet|Sir Harry Smith]] proclaimed British [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] over the territory between the [[s:principality-of-orange|Orange]] and [[e:vaal-river|Vaal]] rivers in February 1848, hoping to control the [[e:boers|Boers]] and keep peace with the [[e:griqua|Griqua]] and [[e:sotho-people|Basotho]]. [[e:andries-pretorius|Andries Pretorius]] rose against the annexation but was defeated at [[e:battle-of-boomplaats|Boomplaats]] in August 1848.
orange-river-sovereignty.r: A British Resident, [[e:henry-douglas-warden|Major Henry Warden]], governed from [[e:bloemfontein|Bloemfontein]] with little money and few troops. His boundary lines between [[e:boers|Boer]] farms and the lands of [[e:moshoeshoe-i|Moshoeshoe]]'s [[s:basotho-kingdom|Basotho Kingdom]] satisfied no one, and British forces were defeated at [[e:battle-of-viervoet|Viervoet]] in 1851 and fought an indecisive battle at [[e:battle-of-berea|Berea]] in 1852. Boer farmers resented taxes and the lack of protection.
orange-river-sovereignty.e: [[e:london|London]] decided the territory was not worth its cost. By the [[e:bloemfontein-convention|Bloemfontein Convention]] of 23 February 1854 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] withdrew, and the [[e:burghers|burghers]] formed the [[s:orange-free-state|Orange Free State]], which kept [[e:bloemfontein|Bloemfontein]] as its capital.
orange-river-sovereignty.re: Dutch Reformed Christianity, Sotho traditional religion

obotrite-confederation.t: A union of Slavic tribes in Mecklenburg whose princes alternated between alliance and war with Franks, Danes and Saxons, founding Mecklenburg's ruling house.
obotrite-confederation.o: The [[e:obotrites|Obotrites]] (Abodrites) were West Slavic tribes who settled the coastlands of [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg]] and [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]] from the 7th century. From around 780 they appear as allies of [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] against the [[s:saxons|Saxons]], and their prince [[e:drasco|Drasco]] helped defeat the Nordalbingian [[e:saxons|Saxons]] in 798.
obotrite-confederation.r: The confederation united several tribes, including the [[e:wagri|Wagrians]] and [[e:polabian-slavs|Polabians]], under princes with strongholds such as [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg]] near [[s:swedish-wismar|Wismar]] and [[e:starigard|Starigard]] ([[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] in [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]]). Trade passed through the port of [[e:reric|Reric]] until the Danish king [[e:gudfred|Godfred]] destroyed it in 808. Princes [[e:gottschalk-obotrite-prince|Gottschalk]] and Henry tried to Christianise the realm; a pagan revolt in 1066 killed Gottschalk.
obotrite-confederation.e: The [[e:wendish-crusade|Wendish Crusade]] of 1147 and the campaigns of [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]] broke Obotrite power; [[e:niklot|Prince Niklot]] was killed in 1160. His son [[e:pribislav-of-mecklenburg|Pribislav]] accepted [[e:saxons|Saxon]] overlordship and [[e:christianity|Christianity]] in 1167, founding the [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Lordship of Mecklenburg]], whose dynasty ruled until 1918.

owari-domain.t: The senior of the three Tokugawa branch houses, ruling from Nagoya castle and entitled to supply an heir if the shogun's line died out.
owari-domain.o: [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] gave [[e:owari-province|Owari]] to his ninth son [[e:tokugawa-yoshinao|Tokugawa Yoshinao]] in 1607. In 1610 Ieyasu ordered lords across [[e:japan|Japan]] to build [[e:nagoya|Nagoya]] castle, and the whole town of [[e:kiyosu|Kiyosu]] was moved there, creating the city of Nagoya.
owari-domain.r: With about 619,500 koku the [[e:owari-province|Owari]] Tokugawa were the highest-ranking of the three [[e:gosanke|Gosanke]] houses, yet no Owari lord ever became [[e:shogun|shogun]]. [[e:tokugawa-muneharu|Tokugawa Muneharu]] defied Shogun [[e:tokugawa-yoshimune|Yoshimune]]'s austerity by encouraging [[e:theatre|theatre]], festivals and commerce, making [[e:nagoya|Nagoya]] thrive, until he was forced to retire in 1739. The domain was rich in [[e:rice|rice]], [[e:timber|timber]] from the Kiso valley and ceramics from [[e:seto-aichi|Seto]].
owari-domain.e: In 1868 [[e:tokugawa-yoshikatsu|Tokugawa Yoshikatsu]] sided with the new government and purged pro-[[e:shogun|shogunate]] retainers. After abolition in 1871 the domain became part of [[e:aichi-prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]].

occupied-japan.t: The Allied occupation of Japan after its defeat in 1945, led by General Douglas MacArthur, which disarmed the country and rebuilt it as a democracy.
occupied-japan.o: [[e:japan|Japan]] accepted the [[e:potsdam-declaration|Potsdam Declaration]] on 15 August 1945 and signed the instrument of surrender on 2 September aboard the [[e:uss-missouri|USS Missouri]]. Allied, overwhelmingly American, forces occupied the home islands under the [[e:supreme-commander-for-the-allied-powers|Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers]], General [[e:douglas-macarthur|Douglas MacArthur]].
occupied-japan.r: The occupation ruled indirectly through the Japanese government and the emperor, who renounced his divinity. It disbanded the armed forces, tried war leaders at the [[e:edo-tokyo|Tokyo]] tribunal, purged officials, broke up the zaibatsu, carried out a sweeping land reform, gave women the vote and in 1947 introduced a new constitution renouncing war. From 1947 a reverse course favoured economic recovery and anti-communism, and the [[e:korean-war|Korean War]] of 1950 turned [[e:japan|Japan]] into a supply base.
occupied-japan.e: The [[e:treaty-of-san-francisco|San Francisco Peace Treaty]], signed in 1951, took effect on 28 April 1952, restoring [[e:japan|Japan's]] [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] alongside a security treaty with the [[s:united-states|United States]]. [[e:okinawa-island|Okinawa]] remained under American control.

ottoman-egypt.t: Egypt as an Ottoman province for nearly three centuries, ruled by pashas from Istanbul while the old Mamluk elite kept real power.
ottoman-egypt.o: [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:selim-i|Selim I]] destroyed the [[s:mamluk-sultanate|Mamluk Sultanate]] at [[e:battle-of-marj-dabiq|Marj Dabiq]] in 1516 and [[e:battle-of-ridaniya|Ridaniya]] in January 1517, then hanged the last [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] sultan [[e:tuman-bay-ii|Tumanbay]] at [[e:cairo|Cairo]]. [[e:egypt|Egypt]] became a province of the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]], governed under the law code issued by Suleiman's grand [[e:vizier|vizier]] [[e:pargali-ibrahim-pasha|Ibrahim Pasha]] in 1525.
ottoman-egypt.r: A pasha appointed from [[e:istanbul|Istanbul]] governed with regiments such as the [[e:janissaries|Janissaries]], but [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] households re-emerged as beys holding key offices. [[e:egypt|Egypt]] supplied grain and tax revenue to Istanbul and controlled the [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] and spice trade of the [[e:red-sea|Red Sea]]. [[e:al-azhar|Al-Azhar]] remained the leading centre of [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] learning. In 1768 [[e:ali-bey-al-kabir|Ali Bey al-Kabir]] briefly declared independence.
ottoman-egypt.e: [[e:napoleon|Bonaparte]]'s invasion in 1798 and the [[s:french-occupation-of-egypt|French occupation of Egypt]] shattered [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] power. In the turmoil after the French left, [[e:muhammad-ali-of-egypt|Muhammad Ali]] was recognised as governor in 1805, beginning [[s:egypt-under-muhammad-ali|Egypt under Muhammad Ali]].

old-kedah.t: The ancient trading kingdom of the Bujang Valley in Kedah, whose temple ruins are the oldest monumental remains in Malaysia.
old-kedah.o: From around the 4th century the estuary of the [[e:merbok-river|Merbok River]] became a landfall for ships crossing the [[e:bay-of-bengal|Bay of Bengal]] from [[e:india|India]]. Inscriptions in [[e:pallava-script|Pallava script]], among them the [[e:buddhagupta-stone|Buddhagupta stone]] naming a sea captain, show Indian merchants settling there. Indian texts call the port Kataha and Tamil sources Kadaram.
old-kedah.r: Over fifty candi, brick and laterite shrines both [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] and Buddhist, have been found in the [[e:bujang-valley|Bujang Valley]], along with [[e:iron-technology|ironworking]] sites at [[e:sungai-batu|Sungai Batu]]. [[s:kedah-sultanate|Kedah]] exported forest goods and [[e:tin|tin]] and redistributed Chinese, Persian and Indian wares. From the 7th century it was closely tied to [[e:srivijaya|Srivijaya]], whose ruler was captured at Kadaram during the [[e:chola-empire|Chola]] raid of 1025.
old-kedah.e: After the [[e:chola-empire|Chola]] attacks the kingdom recovered but declined as trade routes shifted. According to the [[s:kedah-sultanate|Kedah]] annals, its ruler [[e:phra-ong-mahawangsa|Phra Ong Mahawangsa]] converted to [[e:islam|Islam]] in 1136, taking the name Mudzaffar Shah and founding the Kedah Sultanate. The [[e:bujang-valley|Bujang Valley]] sites are now a major archaeological park.

olcades.t: A people of the southern Meseta whose capital Althaia was Hannibal's first conquest as commander in Iberia, in 221 BCE.
olcades.o: The Olcades lived in the upper [[e:guadiana|Guadiana]] and [[e:jucar|Júcar]] region of the southern [[e:meseta-central|Meseta]], probably in modern [[e:cuenca-spain|Cuenca]] and [[e:ciudad-real|Ciudad Real]]. Their origins are obscure, and ancient sources mention them only in connection with the Carthaginian campaigns.
olcades.r: Nothing is known of their institutions beyond their capital, which [[e:polybius|Polybius]] calls Althaia and [[e:livy|Livy]] Cartala, and their wealth in [[e:cattle|cattle]] and grain.
olcades.e: In 221 BCE [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]] attacked them, took Althaia and forced them to pay tribute. The next year Olcadian refugees joined the [[s:carpetani|Carpetani]] and [[s:vaccaei|Vaccaei]] against him at the [[e:tagus|Tagus]] and were defeated. They vanish from the record after this, absorbed into [[s:barcid-iberia|Barcid Iberia]] and later [[e:hispania|Roman Hispania]].

old-pahang-sultanate.t: A Malay sultanate on the east coast of the peninsula, founded by a prince of Malacca in 1470 and joined to Johor in 1623.
old-pahang-sultanate.o: [[e:malacca|Malacca]] conquered [[s:pahang-sultanate|Pahang]], until then a dependency of Siam, in the mid-15th century. Around 1470 [[e:mansur-shah-of-malacca|Sultan Mansur Shah]] of Malacca installed his son [[e:muhammad-shah-of-pahang|Muhammad Shah]] as its first sultan, with his court at [[e:pekan|Pekan]] near the mouth of the [[e:pahang-river|Pahang River]]. The dynasty was thus a branch of the Malacca royal house.
old-pahang-sultanate.r: [[s:pahang-sultanate|Pahang]] exported gold, [[e:tin|tin]] and forest goods, and its rulers kept close ties with [[e:malacca|Malacca]] and, after 1511, with the [[s:johor-sultanate|Johor Sultanate]]. [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:abdul-ghafur-muhiuddin-shah|Abdul Ghafur Muhiuddin Shah]], around 1600, issued a code of law and traded with the [[e:dutch|Dutch]]. Pahang was often caught in the struggle between [[e:johor|Johor]], [[e:aceh|Aceh]] and the Portuguese.
old-pahang-sultanate.e: In 1617 [[e:iskandar-muda|Iskandar Muda]] of the [[s:aceh-sultanate|Aceh Sultanate]] sacked [[s:pahang-sultanate|Pahang]] and carried off its royal family. By 1623 the Pahang line ended and the state passed to the rulers of [[s:johor-sultanate|Johor]]. A new Pahang sultanate emerged only in the 19th century.

onondaga-nation.t: The central nation of the Iroquois Confederacy, keepers of the council fire and the wampum, whose territory near Syracuse still hosts the Grand Council.
onondaga-nation.o: The Onondaga lived in the hills south of [[e:onondaga-lake|Onondaga Lake]] in central [[e:new-york|New York]], near modern [[s:syracuse|Syracuse]]. [[s:iroquois-confederacy|Haudenosaunee]] tradition says their chief [[e:tadodaho|Tadodaho]] was the last and fiercest opponent of [[e:great-peacemaker|the Peacemaker]], and that when he accepted the [[e:great-law-of-peace|Great Law]], his nation was made keeper of the central fire, with Tadodaho as the title of the presiding chief.
onondaga-nation.r: Fourteen Onondaga chiefs sat in the [[e:grand-council-qing|Grand Council]], more than any other nation, and the Onondaga kept the wampum belts that recorded treaties and the [[e:great-law-of-peace|Great Law]]. Their main town moved every few decades as soils and firewood were used up. Seventeenth-century leaders such as [[e:garakontie|Garakontié]] pursued diplomacy with [[s:new-france|New France]], which planted the short-lived [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] mission of [[e:sainte-marie-de-gannentaha|Sainte-Marie de Gannentaha]] on [[e:onondaga-lake|Onondaga Lake]] in 1656.
onondaga-nation.e: In 1779 an American expedition burned the main Onondaga town, and many Onondaga moved to [[e:grand-river-ontario|Grand River]] in [[e:ontario|Ontario]]. In [[e:new-york|New York]] they kept a small territory, which remains under traditional chiefs, issues its own passports and in 2005 sued to recover its [[e:bantustan|homeland]]. [[e:sidney-hill|Sidney Hill]] is the current [[e:tadodaho|Tadodaho]].

odrysian-kingdom.t: The strongest Thracian state, a kingdom stretching from the Aegean to the Danube whose rich tombs and Greek-style city of Seuthopolis survive in Bulgaria.
odrysian-kingdom.o: Around 480 BCE, after the Persian retreat from [[e:europe|Europe]], [[e:teres-i|Teres I]] united Thracian tribes of the [[e:maritsa|Hebrus]] (Maritsa) valley under the [[e:odrysians|Odrysians]]. His son [[e:sitalces|Sitalces]] extended rule from [[s:abdera-800|Abdera]] on the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] to the [[e:danube|Danube]] and allied with [[s:athens|Athens]] at the start of the [[e:peloponnesian-war|Peloponnesian War]].
odrysian-kingdom.r: The king ruled through relatives and tribal princes, drawing tribute from Thracian tribes and Greek coastal cities; [[e:thucydides|Thucydides]] valued the yearly income at some 400 [[e:talent|talents]]. Gold and [[e:silver|silver]] vessels such as the [[e:panagyurishte-treasure|Panagyurishte]] and [[e:rogozen-treasure|Rogozen]] treasures show elite wealth. [[e:cotys-i-odrysian|Cotys I]] strengthened the crown in the 4th century, and [[e:seuthes-iii|Seuthes III]] built [[e:seuthopolis|Seuthopolis]] near [[e:kazanlak|Kazanlak]], where painted tombs survive.
odrysian-kingdom.e: [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II of Macedon]] conquered much of the kingdom after 342 BCE. Odrysian rulers revived under Macedonian and then Roman overlordship as client kings. In 46 CE, after the murder of [[e:rhoemetalces-iii|Rhoemetalces III]], [[e:claudius|Claudius]] annexed the realm as the province of [[e:thrace|Thrace]].

oda-regime.t: The regime of Oda Nobunaga, the warlord who began the unification of Japan, broke the power of Buddhist armies and built the castle of Azuchi.
oda-regime.o: [[e:oda-nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]] inherited part of [[e:owari-province|Owari]] in 1551 and had united the province by 1559. His surprise victory over [[e:imagawa-yoshimoto|Imagawa Yoshimoto]] at [[e:battle-of-okehazama|Okehazama]] in 1560 made his name, and he took [[e:mino-province|Mino]] in 1567, adopting a seal proclaiming rule of the realm by force.
oda-regime.r: In 1568 [[e:oda-nobunaga|Nobunaga]] entered [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]] and installed [[e:ashikaga-yoshiaki|Ashikaga Yoshiaki]] as [[e:shogun|shogun]], then expelled him in 1573. He burned the [[e:enryaku-ji|Enryaku-ji]] on [[e:mount-hiei|Mount Hiei]] in 1571, defeated the [[e:takeda-clan|Takeda]] at [[e:battle-of-nagashino|Nagashino]] in 1575 with massed [[e:musket|muskets]] and fought the [[s:ishiyama-hongan-ji|Ishiyama Hongan-ji]] until 1580. He abolished toll barriers, created free markets, tolerated Christian missionaries and built Azuchi castle on [[e:lake-biwa|Lake Biwa]] from 1576.
oda-regime.e: In 1582 his general [[e:akechi-mitsuhide|Akechi Mitsuhide]] attacked him at the [[e:honno-ji|Honno-ji]] temple in [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]], where [[e:oda-nobunaga|Nobunaga]] died; his heir [[e:oda-nobutada|Nobutada]] was also killed. [[e:toyotomi-hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] defeated Mitsuhide and took over the regime.

omani-empire.t: The Al Bu Said maritime empire of Muscat and Zanzibar, which dominated the Swahili coast and the trade of the western Indian Ocean.
omani-empire.o: In the 1740s [[e:ahmad-ibn-said-al-busaidi|Ahmad ibn Said]], governor of [[e:sohar|Sohar]], expelled the Persian forces that had intervened in the civil war of the [[s:yaaruba-dynasty|Ya'aruba dynasty]] and was elected [[e:imam|imam]]. His family, the [[e:al-bu-said-dynasty|Al Bu Said]], took the title of sayyid and later sultan and made [[e:muscat|Muscat]] their capital.
omani-empire.r: [[e:oman|Oman's]] fleets and merchants controlled trade between [[e:arabia|Arabia]], [[e:persia|Persia]], [[e:india|India]] and [[e:east-africa|East Africa]]. [[e:gwadar|Gwadar]] on the [[s:makran-state|Makran]] coast was acquired in the 1780s and [[e:bandar-abbas|Bandar Abbas]] leased from Persia. [[e:said-bin-sultan|Said ibn Sultan]], ruling from 1806 to 1856, built up [[s:sultanate-of-zanzibar|Zanzibar]], planting [[e:cloves|cloves]] and promoting the caravan trade in [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and slaves, and moved his residence there around 1840. Treaties were signed with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], the [[s:united-states|United States]] and [[e:france|France]].
omani-empire.e: When Said died in 1856 his sons disputed the succession. In 1861 the British-arbitrated [[e:canning-award|Canning Award]] divided the realm into the [[s:sultanate-of-zanzibar|Sultanate of Zanzibar]] and the [[s:sultanate-of-muscat-and-oman|Sultanate of Muscat and Oman]].

ottoman-tripolitania.t: Tripoli as an Ottoman province and corsair base, ruled by pashas and then deys until the Karamanli dynasty took power in 1711.
ottoman-tripolitania.o: The Ottoman fleet captured [[s:county-of-tripoli|Tripoli]] from the [[e:knights-hospitaller|Knights Hospitaller]] in 1551. The corsair [[e:turgut-reis|Turgut Reis]], who had helped take the city, became its governor in 1553 and extended Ottoman authority along the coast and inland, making [[s:tripolitania|Tripolitania]] a province of the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]].
ottoman-tripolitania.r: Pashas sent from [[e:istanbul|Istanbul]] shared power with [[e:janissaries|Janissary]] officers and, from the early 17th century, deys chosen by the garrison. Corsairing in the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] and the trans-Saharan [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] sustained the treasury, and the [[s:sultanate-of-fezzan|Sultanate of Fezzan]] paid tribute. Dey Mehmed Saqizli extended control over [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]] in the 1630s and 1640s.
ottoman-tripolitania.e: Chronic coups between [[e:janissaries|Janissaries]] and pashas ended in 1711, when the cavalry officer [[e:ahmed-karamanli|Ahmed Karamanli]] seized power, killed the Ottoman officials and founded a hereditary dynasty, beginning [[s:karamanli-tripoli|Karamanli Tripoli]].

ogedeid-khanate.t: The Central Asian realm of Ögedei's descendants, whose leader Kaidu waged a forty-year war against Kublai Khan.
ogedeid-khanate.o: [[e:genghis-khan|Genghis Khan]] gave his third son Ögedei pastures in the region of the [[e:emil-river|Emil]] and the upper [[e:irtysh|Irtysh]] in [[s:dzungar-khanate|Dzungaria]]. Ögedei became [[e:great-khan|Great Khan]] in 1229, and his line ruled the [[e:appanage|appanage]]. After the throne passed to the [[e:toluids|Toluids]] in 1251 they were purged, but Ögedei's grandson [[e:kaidu|Kaidu]] rebuilt their power from the 1260s.
ogedeid-khanate.r: [[e:kaidu|Kaidu]] ruled from the Ili and Talas valleys, dominating the [[e:chagatai-khanate|Chagatai Khanate]] through his ally [[e:duwa|Duwa]] and challenging [[e:kublai-khan|Kublai Khan's]] claim to be [[e:great-khan|Great Khan]]. The khanate was a nomadic military power that drew revenue from the oasis towns of [[e:transoxiana|Transoxiana]] and the [[e:tarim-basin|Tarim]], administered by officials such as [[e:masud-beg|Mas'ud Beg]].
ogedeid-khanate.e: [[e:kaidu|Kaidu]] died in 1301 after battle against Yuan forces. His son [[e:chapar|Chapar]] made peace with the Yuan in 1304, but [[e:duwa|Duwa]] turned on him, and by 1310 the [[e:chagatai-khanate|Chagatai Khanate]] had absorbed the Ogedeid lands.

odessa-soviet-republic.t: A Bolshevik republic proclaimed in Odessa in January 1918, which lasted only until the German and Austrian advance in March.
odessa-soviet-republic.o: In January 1918 Bolsheviks and their allies seized [[e:odessa|Odessa]] after street fighting with forces of the [[s:ukrainian-peoples-republic|Ukrainian People's Republic]]. They proclaimed the Odessa Soviet Republic, with [[e:vladimir-yudovsky|Vladimir Yudovsky]] as head of its council of people's commissars, claiming authority over the city and surrounding province.
odessa-soviet-republic.r: The republic relied on [[e:red-guards-russia|Red Guards]] and [[e:black-sea-fleet|Black Sea Fleet]] sailors, imposed levies on the wealthy and carried out arrests and executions. It also fought the [[s:kingdom-of-romania|Kingdom of Romania]], which had occupied [[e:bessarabia|Bessarabia]], and reached a short-lived ceasefire agreement with it. Its control barely extended beyond the city.
odessa-soviet-republic.e: After the [[e:treaty-of-brest-litovsk|Treaty of Brest-Litovsk]], Austro-Hungarian and German troops advanced on [[e:odessa|Odessa]], and the Soviet leaders evacuated the city in March 1918. The republic was nominally merged into the [[e:ukrainian-soviet-republic|Ukrainian Soviet Republic]] and ceased to exist.

orungu-kingdom.t: A Myene-speaking kingdom of the Ogooue delta in Gabon that controlled the slave and later the rubber trade at Cape Lopez.
orungu-kingdom.o: The Orungu established a kingdom around the [[e:ogooue|Ogooue]] delta and [[e:cape-lopez|Cape Lopez]] by the early 18th century, displacing earlier inhabitants. Their position at the mouth of Gabon's largest river gave them control of trade between the interior and European ships.
orungu-kingdom.r: The Orungu king, with a council of clan heads, monopolised trade with Europeans at [[e:cape-lopez|Cape Lopez]], acting as a middleman for slaves supplied from up the [[e:ogooue|Ogooue]]. In the 19th century Cape Lopez became an outlet for an illegal [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] to [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] and [[e:cuba|Cuba]], later replaced by trade in [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]], [[e:ebony|ebony]] and [[e:rubber|rubber]].
orungu-kingdom.e: French influence grew after the 1860s, and the area was absorbed into French [[s:gabon-french-colony|Gabon]]. The kingship declined into a local chieftaincy, which the French ceased to recognise by the late 1920s.

oil-rivers-protectorate.t: The British protectorate over the trading states of the Niger Delta, named for the palm oil that flowed through their creeks to Liverpool.
oil-rivers-protectorate.o: British consul [[e:edward-hewett|Edward Hewett]] signed protection treaties with rulers of the delta states in 1884, ahead of the [[e:berlin-conference|Berlin Conference]], and in June 1885 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] proclaimed the Oil Rivers [[e:protectorate|Protectorate]]. It covered the coast from the [[s:lagos-colony|Lagos Colony]] to the Rio del Rey, including the [[s:bonny-kingdom|Bonny Kingdom]], [[s:kalabari-kingdom|Kalabari Kingdom]], [[s:nembe-kingdom|Nembe Kingdom]], [[s:old-calabar|Old Calabar]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-opobo|Kingdom of Opobo]].
oil-rivers-protectorate.r: For several years British authority was exercised by a consul with few staff, relying on gunboats and on the cooperation of the delta's trading houses. British firms used the [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] to break the middlemen's hold on the [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]] trade. In 1887 consul [[e:harry-johnston|Harry Johnston]] deported [[e:jaja-of-opobo|King Jaja]] of [[s:kingdom-of-opobo|Opobo]], and from 1891 [[e:claude-maxwell-macdonald|Claude MacDonald]], as commissioner and consul-general, set up a proper administration at [[s:old-calabar|Old Calabar]] with customs and courts.
oil-rivers-protectorate.e: In 1893 the [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] was extended inland and renamed the [[s:niger-coast-protectorate|Niger Coast Protectorate]], and in 1900 it became part of the [[s:protectorate-of-southern-nigeria|Protectorate of Southern Nigeria]]. The old delta trading states survived as local authorities under British rule, their kings and house heads reduced to chiefs.

ouchi-clan-domain.t: The realm of the Ouchi lords of western Honshu, who grew rich on trade with Ming China and Korea and made Yamaguchi a little Kyoto.
ouchi-clan-domain.o: The [[e:ouchi-clan|Ouchi]], who claimed descent from a [[s:baekje|Baekje]] prince, were long established in [[e:suo-province|Suo]] province. In the late 14th century [[e:ouchi-yoshihiro|Ouchi Yoshihiro]] held six provinces and controlled trade with [[e:korea|Korea]], but he rebelled against [[e:ashikaga-yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]] and died in 1399; his successors rebuilt the family's power across Suo, [[e:nagato-province|Nagato]] and northern [[e:kyushu|Kyushu]] from about 1400.
ouchi-clan-domain.r: As military governors the [[e:ouchi-clan|Ouchi]] built a strong domain with their own house law. They dominated the official tally trade with [[e:ming-empire|Ming China]] after 1523 and traded with [[s:joseon|Joseon]], using the port of [[e:hakata|Hakata]]. [[e:yamaguchi-city|Yamaguchi]] became a cultural centre where the painter [[e:sesshu-toyo|Sesshu]] worked, and [[e:ouchi-yoshitaka|Ouchi Yoshitaka]] received the [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] [[e:francis-xavier|Francis Xavier]] in 1551.
ouchi-clan-domain.e: In 1551 the retainer [[e:sue-harukata|Sue Harukata]] overthrew [[e:ouchi-yoshitaka|Yoshitaka]], who killed himself, and set up a puppet lord. [[e:mori-motonari|Mori Motonari]] defeated Sue at [[e:battle-of-miyajima|Itsukushima]] in 1555 and destroyed the last [[e:ouchi-clan|Ouchi]] in 1557, taking over their lands.

oretani.t: An Iberian people of the upper Guadalquivir whose city Castulo controlled the silver mines of the Sierra Morena and gave Hannibal his wife.
oretani.o: The Oretani lived in the upper [[e:guadalquivir|Guadalquivir]] valley and the southern [[e:meseta-central|Meseta]], in modern [[e:jaen|Jaén]] and [[e:ciudad-real|Ciudad Real]], from the mid-first millennium BCE. They took their name from the town of Oretum, but their leading city was [[e:castulo|Castulo]] near [[e:linares|Linares]], a crossroads between the coast and the interior.
oretani.r: Their wealth came from the [[e:silver|silver]] and lead mines of the [[e:sierra-morena|Sierra Morena]], exploited intensively under Carthaginian and then Roman control. [[e:castulo|Castulo]] had rich princely tombs and later minted bronze coins with an Iberian legend. [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]] married [[e:himilce|Himilce]], said to be a princess of Castulo, tying the Oretani to [[s:barcid-iberia|Barcid Iberia]].
oretani.e: In 206 BCE [[e:castulo|Castulo]] went over to [[e:rome|Rome]] during the Scipionic campaigns. The Oretani joined the revolt of 197 BCE but were absorbed into [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]] and later [[s:hispania-tarraconensis|Tarraconensis]], and Castulo remained an important Roman mining town.

oriental-republic-of-uruguay.t: The small republic between Argentina and Brazil, created as a buffer state in 1828, which built one of the earliest welfare states in the Americas.
oriental-republic-of-uruguay.o: The [[e:preliminary-peace-convention|Preliminary Peace Convention]] of 1828, mediated by [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], ended the [[e:cisplatine-war|Cisplatine War]] between [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] and the [[s:united-provinces-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|United Provinces of the Río de la Plata]] and made the former [[s:cisplatina|Cisplatina]] an independent state. Its first constitution was sworn on 18 July 1830, and [[e:fructuoso-rivera|Fructuoso Rivera]] became the first president.
oriental-republic-of-uruguay.r: Politics were long dominated by two parties, the [[e:national-party-uruguay|Blancos]] and [[e:colorado-party-uruguay|Colorados]], whose rivalry led to the [[e:uruguayan-civil-war|Guerra Grande]] of 1839 to 1851, with a nine-year siege of [[e:montevideo|Montevideo]]. Immigration from [[e:spain|Spain]] and [[e:italy|Italy]] and exports of beef and wool brought prosperity. [[e:jose-batlle-y-ordonez|José Batlle y Ordóñez]], president in the early 20th century, introduced social welfare, secular education and the eight-hour day. Political violence involving the [[e:tupamaros|Tupamaros]] [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrillas]] preceded a military dictatorship from 1973 to 1985.
oriental-republic-of-uruguay.e: Democracy returned in 1985, and the left-wing [[e:broad-front-uruguay|Frente Amplio]] governed from 2005 to 2020 under [[e:tabare-vazquez|Tabaré Vázquez]] and [[e:jose-mujica|José Mujica]], legalising cannabis in 2013, and returned to power in 2025 under [[e:yamandu-orsi|Yamandú Orsi]]. [[e:uruguay|Uruguay]] ranks among [[e:latin-america|Latin America's]] most stable democracies.

old-calabar.t: Efik trading towns on the Calabar river, governed by the Ekpe society and major ports of the slave and palm oil trades.
old-calabar.o: The [[e:efik|Efik]] settled on the [[e:calabar|Calabar]] river in the 17th century, founding [[e:creek-town|Creek Town]], Old Town and [[e:duke-town|Duke Town]], which Europeans called Old Calabar. They became middlemen between European ships and the peoples of the [[e:cross-river|Cross river]] hinterland, from whom they bought slaves.
old-calabar.r: There was no single king; the towns were ruled by heads of trading houses and by [[e:ekpe|Ekpe]], the leopard society, which made laws, enforced debts and bound European traders. The diary of the trader [[e:antera-duke|Antera Duke]] from the 1780s records life in [[e:duke-town|Duke Town]]. After abolition, [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]] replaced slaves, and Scottish Presbyterian missionaries arrived in 1846.
old-calabar.e: The [[e:efik|Efik]] chiefs signed a British protection treaty in 1884, and [[e:calabar|Calabar]] became the capital of the [[s:oil-rivers-protectorate|Oil Rivers Protectorate]] and then the [[s:niger-coast-protectorate|Niger Coast Protectorate]]. It is now the capital of [[e:cross-river-state|Cross River State]], where the [[e:obong-of-calabar|Obong of Calabar]] reigns.

ozolian-locris.t: Confederation of the western Locrians on the Gulf of Corinth, centred on Amphissa, whose clash with the Amphictyony brought Philip II into central Greece.
ozolian-locris.o: The western or Ozolian [[e:locrians|Locrians]] lived on the northern shore of the [[e:gulf-of-corinth|Gulf of Corinth]], west of [[s:delphi|Delphi]], in small hill towns such as Amphissa, [[e:chaleion|Chaleion]] and [[e:oeantheia|Oeanthea]]. They were related to the Locrians of [[s:opuntian-locris|Opuntian Locris]] but separated by [[e:phocis|Phocis]] and [[e:doris-greece|Doris]]. [[e:nafpaktos|Naupactus]] was theirs until [[s:athens|Athens]] gave it to Messenian refugees c. 456 BCE.
ozolian-locris.r: [[e:thucydides|Thucydides]] described the western [[e:locrians|Locrians]] as still carrying arms in daily life, a sign of archaic customs. Their towns were loosely confederated, with Amphissa the most important. A bronze tablet from [[e:chaleion|Chaleion]] of the 5th century BCE regulates disputes between towns, a rare early example of Greek inter-state law.
ozolian-locris.e: When Amphissa farmed the sacred plain of [[s:delphi|Delphi]], the Amphictyony declared the Fourth Sacred War; [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]] destroyed Amphissa in 338 BCE. Western [[e:locris|Locris]] later joined the [[s:aetolian-league|Aetolian League]] and came under [[e:rome|Rome]] in 146 BCE.

orchha-state.t: The Bundela Rajput kingdom of Bundelkhand, whose riverside capital of palaces and temples was built by Bir Singh Deo, an ally of the emperor Jahangir.
orchha-state.o: In 1531 the [[e:bundelas|Bundela]] chief [[e:rudra-pratap-singh|Rudra Pratap Singh]] founded Orchha on an island in the [[e:betwa-river|Betwa]] river and made it his capital. The [[e:bundela|Bundela Rajputs]] had risen in the region after the decline of the [[s:chandela-dynasty|Chandela dynasty]].
orchha-state.r: Orchha's rulers resisted and then served the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]]. [[e:vir-singh-deo|Bir Singh Deo]] had [[e:akbar|Akbar's]] minister [[e:abul-fazl-ibn-mubarak|Abul Fazl]] killed in 1602 on behalf of [[e:jahangir|Prince Salim]], the future Jahangir, and was rewarded with power and wealth; he built the [[e:jahangir-mahal|Jahangir Mahal]] and many temples. The [[e:ram-raja-temple|Ram Raja temple]] made Orchha a pilgrimage centre. In 1783 the capital moved to [[e:tikamgarh|Tikamgarh]].
orchha-state.e: Orchha signed a treaty with the British in 1812. In 1950 it joined [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]], which merged into [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956. The old capital's palaces and cenotaphs are major monuments.

obock.t: France's first foothold on the Gulf of Aden, a small coaling station that grew into the colony of French Somaliland and modern Djibouti.
obock.o: In 1862 French agents bought the anchorage of Obock on the northern shore of the Gulf of [[s:sultanate-of-tadjoura|Tadjoura]] from local [[e:afar|Afar]] rulers for 10,000 thalers. [[e:france|France]] had little use for it until the 1880s, when the opening of the [[e:suez-canal|Suez Canal]] and [[e:britain|Britain's]] refusal to [[e:coal|coal]] French ships at [[e:aden|Aden]] made a French base necessary.
obock.r: In 1884 [[e:leonce-lagarde|Leonce Lagarde]] became commandant and expanded French influence by treaties with the [[s:sultanate-of-tadjoura|Sultanate of Tadjoura]] and [[e:issa-clan|Issa Somali]] clans. Obock served as a coaling and supply station for French ships bound for [[e:indochina|Indochina]] and [[e:madagascar|Madagascar]]. Its harbour was poor, and its trade was small.
obock.e: [[e:leonce-lagarde|Lagarde]] founded [[s:djibouti|Djibouti]] across the gulf in 1888, which offered a better port and access to the Ethiopian trade. In 1896 the capital moved there and Obock became part of [[s:french-somaliland|French Somaliland]].

osismii.t: Gallic people of the far western tip of Brittany, the end of the known world for Greek and Roman geographers.
osismii.o: The Osismii lived in [[e:finistere|Finistère]] and western [[e:cotes-darmor|Côtes-d'Armor]]. The Greek explorer [[e:pytheas|Pytheas]] probably referred to them as the Ostimioi around 320 BCE, placing them on a promontory facing the Ocean. Caesar lists them among the Armorican peoples.
osismii.r: Their economy rested on farming, fishing and sea trade along the Atlantic route to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]]. No ruler or central town is recorded before the conquest.
osismii.e: They submitted to [[e:publius-licinius-crassus|Publius Crassus]] in 57 BCE and supported the [[s:veneti|Veneti]] in 56 BCE. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] their capital was [[e:carhaix-plouguer|Vorgium]] (Carhaix). In late antiquity their land was settled by migrants from [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and became part of [[s:domnonee|Domnonée]] and [[s:cornouaille|Cornouaille]].

organisation-of-western-continental-gree.t: Regional revolutionary government of western mainland Greece in 1821-1822, organised by Alexandros Mavrokordatos at Missolonghi.
organisation-of-western-continental-gree.o: Western mainland [[e:greece|Greece]], from the [[e:gulf-of-corinth|Gulf of Corinth]] to [[e:epirus|Epirus]], rose against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] in the spring of 1821. In November 1821 the [[e:phanariotes|Phanariot]] politician [[e:alexandros-mavrokordatos|Alexandros Mavrokordatos]] gathered local representatives at [[e:missolonghi|Missolonghi]], where they adopted a charter and created a senate to govern the region and coordinate the military chieftains.
organisation-of-western-continental-gree.r: The organisation had a senate of local notables and military leaders, with [[e:alexandros-mavrokordatos|Mavrokordatos]] as president. It raised revenue, supplied armed bands and tried to restrain the chieftains, many of whom had served as armatoloi under the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]]. [[e:missolonghi|Missolonghi]], a lagoon town, became the region's centre and later the scene of famous sieges.
organisation-of-western-continental-gree.e: With the First [[e:national-assembly-of-france|National Assembly]] at [[s:epidaurus|Epidaurus]] in January 1822 and the founding of the [[s:first-hellenic-republic|First Hellenic Republic]], regional bodies were placed under the central government and were abolished during 1822. [[e:alexandros-mavrokordatos|Mavrokordatos]] became president of the national executive.
