ober-ost.t: German military state in occupied Lithuania, Courland and western Belarus during the First World War, run by Hindenburg and Ludendorff's staff.
ober-ost.o: After the German offensives of 1915 drove Russian armies out of [[e:courland|Courland]], [[s:republic-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] and the Grodno-Białystok region, the territory was placed under the Supreme Commander in the East, Oberbefehlshaber Ost, [[e:paul-von-hindenburg|Paul von Hindenburg]], with [[e:erich-ludendorff|Erich Ludendorff]] as chief of staff. The headquarters moved to [[e:kaunas|Kovno]] (Kaunas).
ober-ost.r: Ober Ost was a military administration that tried to remake the land according to German plans: it requisitioned food, [[e:timber|timber]] and livestock, imposed forced labour and controlled movement through passes. It also sponsored newspapers, schools and surveys among [[e:lithuanians|Lithuanians]], [[e:latvians|Latvians]], [[e:poles|Poles]], [[e:jews|Jews]] and [[e:belarusians|Belarusians]], seeing the region as a German colony.
ober-ost.e: After the [[e:treaty-of-brest-litovsk|Treaty of Brest-Litovsk]] in March 1918, [[e:germany|Germany]] allowed client institutions, including the Lithuanian [[e:council-of-lithuania|Taryba]], which had declared independence in February 1918, and planned a [[s:duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia-1918|Duchy of Courland and Semigallia]] (1918). Germany's defeat in November 1918 ended the administration, and the [[s:republic-of-lithuania-1918-1940|Republic of Lithuania]] and [[s:republic-of-latvia|Republic of Latvia]] emerged.
ober-ost.re: Lutheran and Catholic Christianity, Judaism, Orthodoxy

ostrogothic-kingdom.t: Gothic kingdom of Theodoric the Great in Italy, which preserved Roman government and culture before Justinian's armies destroyed it.
ostrogothic-kingdom.o: The [[e:ostrogoths|Ostrogoths]], settled in the [[e:balkans|Balkans]] as federates of the eastern empire, were sent to [[e:italy|Italy]] by the emperor [[e:zeno-emperor|Zeno]] under their king [[e:theodoric-the-great|Theodoric]]. They invaded in 489, besieged [[e:odoacer|Odoacer]] in [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]] and killed him in 493, and Theodoric became ruler of Italy under nominal imperial authority.
ostrogothic-kingdom.r: [[e:theodoric-the-great|Theodoric]] governed through Roman officials and the Senate, while the [[e:goths|Goths]] formed the army and kept their Arian faith. [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] such as [[e:cassiodorus|Cassiodorus]] and [[e:boethius|Boethius]] served him, though he executed Boethius in 524. [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]] gained [[e:santapollinare-nuovo|Sant'Apollinare Nuovo]] and his mausoleum. His realm reached into [[s:county-of-provence|Provence]], [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]] and the [[e:alps|Alps]], and he led a network of Germanic kingdoms through marriage alliances.
ostrogothic-kingdom.e: After [[e:theodoric-the-great|Theodoric]]'s death in 526, the murder of his daughter [[e:amalasuntha|Amalasuntha]] gave Justinian a pretext to invade in 535. [[e:belisarius|Belisarius]] and [[e:narses|Narses]] fought the [[e:goths|Goths]] for almost twenty years, leaving [[e:italy|Italy]] devastated. [[e:totila|Totila]] was killed at [[e:battle-of-taginae|Busta Gallorum]] in 552, and [[e:teia|Teia]] at [[e:battle-of-mons-lactarius|Mons Lactarius]] in 552 or 553.

onogurs.t: Oghur Turkic nomads of the Pontic steppe whose name survives in the word 'Hungary', and from whom the Bulgars of Kubrat emerged.
onogurs.o: The Onogurs, meaning 'ten [[e:oghurs|Oghurs]]', are first recorded in 463 when, with the [[e:saragurs|Saragurs]] and [[e:urogs|Urogs]], they sent envoys to [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] after being driven west by the [[s:sabirs|Sabirs]]. They settled in the steppe between the Kuban, the [[e:sea-of-azov|Sea of Azov]] and the lower [[e:don-river|Don]], in contact with the [[e:caucasus|Caucasus]] and Byzantine [[e:crimea|Crimea]].
onogurs.r: They were a tribal confederation of pastoral nomads organised into ten tribes under chieftains. Byzantine writers record their dealings with [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] and their conversion attempts; their leader [[e:organa|Organa]] and his nephew [[e:kubrat|Kubrat]] had ties to the Byzantine court. In the late 6th century they came under the [[s:western-turkic-khaganate|Western Turkic Khaganate]], alongside the [[s:utigurs|Utigurs]] and [[s:kutrigurs|Kutrigurs]].
onogurs.e: Around 632 [[e:kubrat|Kubrat]] threw off Turkic rule and united Onogurs, [[s:utigurs|Utigurs]] and [[s:kutrigurs|Kutrigurs]] as [[s:old-great-bulgaria|Old Great Bulgaria]]. After his death the [[e:khazar-khaganate|Khazars]] scattered it, and his sons led groups to the [[e:danube|Danube]] and [[e:volga|Volga]]. The Onogur name, through Slavic and [[e:latin|Latin]], gave [[e:europe|Europe]] its name for the [[e:magyars|Hungarians]].

orchomenus-arcadia.t: Ancient hill city of northern Arcadia, a rival of Mantinea that refused to join the Arcadian League.
orchomenus-arcadia.o: Orchomenus occupied a hill between two upland plains in northern [[e:arcadia|Arcadia]]. Tradition made it the seat of early Arcadian kings; the last, Aristocrates, was said to have been stoned for betraying the [[e:messenians|Messenians]] to [[s:sparta|Sparta]] in the 7th century BCE. [[e:homer|Homer]] called it 'rich in flocks'.
orchomenus-arcadia.r: Orchomenus was an ally of [[s:sparta|Sparta]] in the [[s:peloponnesian-league|Peloponnesian League]] and a rival of [[s:mantinea|Mantinea]], with which it fought over land and leadership in [[e:arcadia|Arcadia]]. It sent troops to [[e:battle-of-thermopylae|Thermopylae]] and [[s:plataea|Plataea]]. In 370 BCE it refused to join the new [[s:arcadian-league|Arcadian League]] dominated by Mantinea and [[s:tegea|Tegea]].
orchomenus-arcadia.e: In the [[e:hellenistic-period|Hellenistic period]] Orchomenus was taken in turn by the [[s:aetolian-league|Aetolian League]], [[s:sparta|Sparta]] and the [[s:achaean-league|Achaean League]], and [[e:antigonus-iii-doson|Antigonus Doson]] of the [[s:antigonid-kingdom-of-macedonia|Antigonid Kingdom of Macedonia]] captured it in 223 BCE. It passed under [[e:rome|Rome]] in 146 BCE.

occupied-enemy-territory-administration.t: The British-led military government of the former Ottoman Levant after the First World War, which preceded the French and British mandates.
occupied-enemy-territory-administration.o: After General [[e:edmund-allenby|Allenby]]'s forces took [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] in December 1917 and conquered the rest of the [[e:levant|Levant]] in 1918, the occupied Ottoman territories were placed under military administration as Occupied Enemy Territory, as [[e:international-law|international law]] required until a peace settlement.
occupied-enemy-territory-administration.r: The territory was divided into zones: OETA South, roughly [[e:palestine|Palestine]], under British officers; OETA East, inland [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] and [[s:emirate-of-transjordan|Transjordan]], administered by Faisal's Arab government; and [[s:french-cilicia|OETA North]] (or West), the coast, under French officers. The administration preserved Ottoman law, restored supplies after wartime famine and began reconstruction. [[e:ronald-storrs|Ronald Storrs]] served as military governor of [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]].
occupied-enemy-territory-administration.e: In 1920 the [[e:san-remo-conference|San Remo conference]] assigned [[e:league-of-nations-mandate|mandates]] to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:france|France]]. OETA South was replaced by a civil administration under [[e:herbert-samuel|Herbert Samuel]] in July 1920, forming [[s:mandatory-palestine|Mandatory Palestine]], while France occupied inland [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] after defeating the [[s:arab-kingdom-of-syria|Arab Kingdom of Syria]].
